title: Backyard Dig Turns Up Huge Viking Silver Treasure
summary:
A homeowner in northern Denmark was clearing ground for a new terrace. Instead of just rocks and grass, the person found the largest silver hoard ever discovered in Denmark. It weighs more than 40 pounds.

After about half an hour of digging, a tool hit something strange. Hand digging turned up jewelry, coins, and silver bars. The finder called museums right away.

Archaeologists led by Torben Sarauw carefully dug the yard. They found about 700 silver objects. The treasure had been kept in a clay pot. The top broke long ago, so some pieces spilled into the soil.

The hoard includes silver bars, rings, and "hack-silver" bits Vikings used like coins. There are also English and Arabic coins and a tiny Thor's hammer charm. Experts think it was buried in the 10th century. Danish law says the treasure goes to the National Museum, and the finder gets a reward.
why_it_matters: Everyday digging can uncover history that museums share with everyone, including kids.
